B1:
Touched fires once per touching part and often several times in the same frame (both feet, legs, HumanoidRootPart). Those events are already queued (and with Deferred SignalBehavior they all still run) before part:Destroy() takes effect, so 3-5 handlers each add 10. Fix: a debounce flag set before any work, and disconnect:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local collected = false
local conn
conn = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	if collected then return end
	local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if not plr then return end
	local ls = plr:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local coins = ls and ls:FindFirstChild("Coins")
	if not coins then return end
	collected = true
	conn:Disconnect()
	coins.Value += 10
	part:Destroy()
end)
```
For many coins, use one CollectionService tag-driven script instead of a Script per coin; for per-player coins, track collected sets per player.
B2:
With StreamingEnabled the client only has instances near the player; far doors (or ancestors like Hotel) aren't streamed in yet, and can stream out later, so direct indexing at startup throws. Fix 1: wait for it: `local hotel = workspace.Map.Buildings:WaitForChild("Hotel", 10)` then `hotel and hotel:WaitForChild("Door", 10)`, handle nil, and set the Hotel model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic so it arrives whole (or Persistent if it must always exist, at a memory cost). Fix 2 (better): tag doors with CollectionService and bind as they stream in/out:
```lua
local CS = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local conns = {}
local function add(d) if not conns[d] then conns[d] = d.Touched:Connect(onTouch) end end
CS:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door"):Connect(add)
CS:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("Door"):Connect(function(d)
	if conns[d] then conns[d]:Disconnect() conns[d] = nil end
end)
for _, d in CS:GetTagged("Door") do add(d) end
```
Also consider handling gameplay door touches on the server, where everything exists. Don't fix it by turning streaming off.
B3: Bugs: (1) plr may be nil (player left) -> error inside pcall, yet PurchaseGranted is returned: charged, nothing. (2) The pcall result `ok` is ignored: any DataStore failure still returns PurchaseGranted. (3) No idempotency: ProcessReceipt can be re-invoked for the same PurchaseId (retry after timeout, rejoin, server crash); each call adds 100 -> double coins. (4) GetAsync + SetAsync is non-atomic; races with the session's own save or other servers can overwrite or lose coins; use UpdateAsync (or the session-locked profile). (5) Writing the store directly while the live session also holds coins means the next autosave can overwrite it. Correct behaviour: if the player is not in the server or data isn't loaded, return NotProcessedYet. In one atomic update check whether info.PurchaseId is already in the player's processed list; if not, add 100 coins and record the PurchaseId (cap list length). Return PurchaseGranted only if the save succeeded; on any failure return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries. Exactly one ProcessReceipt handler, dispatching by ProductId.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized: tables are copied as plain data and metatables are stripped, so the client gets {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30} without __index, and w.Fire is nil (functions can't be sent either). Instances are sent as references; ServerStorage contents never replicate to clients, so the reference arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data and rebuild on the client from a shared class module in ReplicatedStorage: `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` (or Weapon.new(data)). For the part, move it (or a template) to ReplicatedStorage/Workspace so the client has it, or send an identifier or the needed properties (CFrame, name) instead. Also avoid mixed-key tables and non-string dictionary keys over remotes.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's direction vector is also the ray's length. .Unit has length 1, so the ray only checks 1 stud from origin and misses almost everything. It can also hit the shooter's own character/gun first. Fix:
```lua
local RANGE = 300
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { shooterCharacter }
local offset = target - origin
if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, offset.Unit * RANGE, params) -- or offset for exact distance
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
Guard against target == origin (Unit of zero vector is NaN). Do authoritative hit validation on the server.
B6: When the last player leaves, the server starts shutting down; the PlayerRemoving handler yields on SetAsync and the server can close before the request completes, so the save is dropped (same on shutdowns for updates). Standard fix: game:BindToClose(function() ... end) that saves every remaining player's data in parallel (task.spawn per player, then wait until all finish) within the ~30 second limit. PlayerRemoving and BindToClose share one save function with a per-player saving/saved guard so they don't double-save. Use UpdateAsync with a session lock rather than SetAsync, retry with backoff, and autosave periodically (every 1-5 min) so a crash loses little.
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local Abilities = require(game.ServerScriptService.Abilities) -- [id] = function(player, char)
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: { [Player]: number } = {}

UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
	if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" or not Abilities[abilityId] then return end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastUse[player]
	if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
	local char = player.Character
	local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	lastUse[player] = now -- set before any yield
	Abilities[abilityId](player, char)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)
```
The cooldown is server-authoritative (server clock only); any client cooldown UI is cosmetic.
B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData_v1")
local GEMS100 = 123456
local MAX_RECEIPTS = 100

local handlers = {
	[GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end,
}

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
	local grant = handlers[info.ProductId]
	if not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
	if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on rejoin
	local ok, err = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, "u_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
		data = data or { Gems = 0, Receipts = {} }
		data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
		if table.find(data.Receipts, info.PurchaseId) then return data end -- already granted
		grant(data)
		table.insert(data.Receipts, info.PurchaseId)
		if #data.Receipts > MAX_RECEIPTS then table.remove(data.Receipts, 1) end
		return data
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("Receipt save failed:", err)
		return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
	end
	-- refresh the live session cache / leaderstats from the saved value here
	return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
The transform is pure (no yields or side effects). Only this one script sets ProcessReceipt. With a session-locked profile, apply grant + PurchaseId to the profile and return Granted only after it saves; never write the same key from two places.
B9:
```lua
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local info = TweenInfo.new(0.4, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local SHOWN = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
local HIDDEN = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1.5)
local current: Tween?

local function play(goal: UDim2): Tween
	if current then current:Cancel() end
	current = TweenService:Create(menu, info, { Position = goal })
	current:Play()
	return current
end

local function open()
	menu.Position = HIDDEN
	menu.Visible = true
	play(SHOWN)
end

local function close()
	local t = play(HIDDEN)
	t.Completed:Once(function(state)
		if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then
			menu.Visible = false -- only after the slide finished
		end
	end)
end
```
(menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5) for centred positions.) Checking PlaybackState stops a cancelled close (menu reopened mid-slide) from hiding it.
B10:
```lua
local MAX_RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
	if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end -- NaN guard
	local char = player.Character
	local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
	local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
	local offset = targetPos - head.Position
	if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { char }
	local result = workspace:Raycast(head.Position, offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE, params)
	if not result then return end
	local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
		hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
	end
	return result
end
```
Call from a validated, rate-limited remote; the server casts from its own head position instead of trusting a client hit. Accessories and tool parts resolve to the character via FindFirstAncestorOfClass.
B11:
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local connections: { [BasePart]: RBXScriptConnection } = {}

local function onAdded(inst)
	if not inst:IsA("BasePart") or connections[inst] then return end
	connections[inst] = inst.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local model = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
		local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
		if hum and hum.Health > 0 then
			hum.Health = 0
		end
	end)
end

local function onRemoved(inst)
	local c = connections[inst]
	if c then
		c:Disconnect()
		connections[inst] = nil
	end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved) -- also fires when destroyed
for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do
	onAdded(inst)
end
```
Connect the signals before iterating GetTagged so nothing added in between is missed; the guard prevents double connections.
B12:
```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_ATTEMPTS, RETRY_DELAY = 3, 2
local retries: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function safeTeleport(placeId: number, players: { Player }, teleportData: any?)
	local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
	if teleportData ~= nil then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
	local ok, result
	for attempt = 1, MAX_ATTEMPTS do
		ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
		if ok then return true, result end
		warn(("Teleport attempt %d failed: %s"):format(attempt, tostring(result)))
		task.wait(RETRY_DELAY * attempt)
	end
	return false, result
end

TeleportService.TeleportInitFailed:Connect(function(player, result, message, placeId, options)
	if result == Enum.TeleportResult.IsTeleporting then return end
	local n = (retries[player] or 0) + 1
	if n > MAX_ATTEMPTS then retries[player] = nil warn("Teleport gave up:", message) return end
	retries[player] = n
	task.wait(RETRY_DELAY * n)
	if player.Parent then
		pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, { player }, options)
	end
end)
game:GetService("Players").PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) retries[p] = nil end)
```
TeleportAsync is server-only; save data (release the session lock) before teleporting. Teleport data passes through the client: never put coins or trusted state in it.
B13: (a) Buying: client -> server via a RemoteEvent (or a client-invoked RemoteFunction, InvokeServer, if the UI wants an immediate success/fail result). The client sends only the item id; the server validates (types, rate limit, item exists, price from a server catalog, enough coins), deducts and grants. The balance lives in server-owned, session-locked player data saved to DataStores; never trust a client value. (b) Counter update: server -> client by replicated state (leaderstats IntValue or a player attribute the client watches with GetAttributeChangedSignal) or a RemoteEvent FireClient carrying the new authoritative balance. Don't use RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server thread yields until the client returns, and a client may never return (exploiter, lag, disconnect) or error, so the server's purchase flow can hang or break; the server should never wait on a client. One-way fires or replicated values are safe.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData; read via Player:GetJoinData() on the server) travels through the client, so it can be read and tampered with; it is size-limited and lost if the teleport fails. Fine for non-sensitive hints (chosen loadout ids, match/party id) as long as the destination server validates them (does the player own that loadout?). Never put coin balances in it. DataStores are the durable source of truth for coins: save and release the session lock before teleporting, load in the match place with session locking and retries (places in one experience share DataStores). MemoryStores (hash maps/sorted maps/queues) are fast, server-only, expiring storage, good for short-lived handoff state (match assignment, loadout, reserved server code) keyed by userId with a TTL, but not durable, so not for currency. Choice: coins in the DataStore profile; loadout in the saved profile or via MemoryStore/teleport data, always validated server-side against owned items.
B15: Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): duplicated code that diverges, one bug fixed 610 times, more threads/connections/memory and startup cost, and copies inside cloned or streamed models run unpredictably. Tag-driven: tag instances (Door, Pickup, Turret) with CollectionService and have one system per type (a server Script/ModuleScript) that binds behaviour: for _, inst in CS:GetTagged(tag) do setup(inst) end, plus CS:GetInstanceAddedSignal(tag):Connect(setup) and GetInstanceRemovedSignal(tag):Connect(cleanup), storing connections per instance (Maid/Janitor) and disconnecting on removal. Per-instance config via attributes (OpenTime, Damage, Range). The server owns authoritative logic (door state, pickup grants, turret targeting using one shared update loop over all turrets rather than 60 loops); client systems do visuals. Newly spawned instances just carry the tag (clones keep tags) and are picked up by the added signal; with StreamingEnabled the client's added/removed signals fire as instances stream in and out, so client code handles streaming naturally. Use Atomic models for multi-part doors/turrets.
B16: Give the driver's client network ownership of the car (VehicleSeat does this for the occupant, or SetNetworkOwner(driver) when they sit and back to the server when they leave). Physics then runs locally with no input latency, which racing needs; server-owned cars feel laggy. Risk: the owner is authoritative over that assembly's physics, so an exploiter can set its CFrame/velocity: teleport, speed hack, fly, skip checkpoints, fling others. The server must still validate: speed/acceleration caps vs the car's stats, position deltas per tick (teleports), checkpoints passed in order with plausible timing, server-recorded lap/finish times, staying on/near the track, and anything affecting other players (collisions, damage). On violation, reset/rubberband or reclaim ownership (SetNetworkOwner(nil)). Disable automatic ownership while driven. Server Authority (AuthorityMode = Server, 2026) is an option for server-validated predicted physics.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the continuous aim/position stream (and let replicated character physics carry position where possible, sending only aim). Constraints: delivery isn't guaranteed and order isn't preserved (packets can drop or arrive out of order), and payload size is limited (about 900 bytes per call; larger ones are dropped). Handle it: send only the latest absolute state (never deltas or must-arrive events); include a sequence number or timestamp and ignore stale packets; keep payloads tiny (quantize angles/positions, pack with buffer); lower the rate to 10-20 Hz and send only on meaningful change; interpolate on receivers. Keep one-off important events (fire, reload, hit claims) on a reliable, rate-limited RemoteEvent. The server still validates values (finite, plausible vs server-known position) and rate-limits per player.
B18: Split NPCs into several Actors (a Script under each Actor managing a batch, e.g. 4-16 Actors, or the NPC model as the Actor). Run the heavy reads in parallel with RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize()): workspace:Raycast/spatial queries and path scoring are safe in parallel. Then task.synchronize() to apply results (move humanoids, set properties, fire remotes) in the serial phase. Limits: in parallel you may only read most of the DataModel and call thread-safe APIs; writing properties, creating/destroying instances, yielding calls and unsafe APIs (e.g. PathfindingService:ComputeAsync, which yields) must be serial; each Actor is its own Luau VM, so module state isn't shared (require gives separate copies); share via SharedTable, Actor:SendMessage/BindToMessage or attributes; scripts must be descendants of an Actor; too many tiny Actors add overhead, too few limit parallelism; results apply a phase/frame later. Also cut work: time-slice NPCs across frames, lower update rates for distant/idle NPCs, cache paths and recompute only when needed. Profile with the MicroProfiler.
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Sensible settings: StreamingTargetRadius near the default 1024 (lower, e.g. 512-768, for dense mobile-heavy maps), StreamingMinRadius default 64 (raise a bit for fast movement), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic so far content unloads (LowMemory only streams out under pressure), StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause) so players don't fall into unloaded areas. Per model: ModelStreamingMode = Atomic for things that must arrive whole (doors, NPC rigs, vehicles), Persistent only for the few things scripts must always see (sparingly), Default/Nonatomic for scenery; LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for distant landmarks. Before server-side teleports, player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position). Scripts: client code can't assume instances exist: replace direct indexing with WaitForChild plus timeouts (handle nil), or better CollectionService tags with GetInstanceAddedSignal/RemovedSignal so code binds and cleans up as things stream in and out; don't hold references to streamed-out parts. Server sees everything, so keep authoritative logic there. Test with streaming in Studio and on low-end phones.
B20: Each SetAsync is a write. 80 players x 12 per minute = 960 writes/min from one server, more than the per-server write budget (60 + 10 x players = 860/min) and a big share of the per-experience write budget (300 + 20 x CCU), so requests queue; when the queue is full, further calls are dropped (error 302: set request dropped, queue full) and saves are lost. Writing the same key every 5 s also hits per-key throughput limits. Better: keep data in a server-side session cache; autosave each player every 60-300 s, staggered across the interval, and only when dirty; save on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose; use UpdateAsync with a session lock instead of SetAsync; pcall with exponential backoff; check DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType and defer non-critical saves when low; one combined key per player. ProfileStore implements this.

Connect a client via Quick connect (Assistant Settings > MCP Servers; lists Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Antigravity), a JSON config entry, or a CLI command; restart the client after config edits. B22: Three core instances: InputContext (a group of actions you enable/disable and prioritise: Enabled, Priority, Sink), InputAction (one logical action; Type = Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D, Direction3D or ViewportPosition), and InputBinding (maps a device input to the action: KeyCode, PrimaryModifier/SecondaryModifier for chords, UIButton for on-screen touch buttons, Scale). Bindings are children of actions, actions children of contexts. A Bool action signals a press through its Pressed and Released events, StateChanged(newState), and GetState() for polling. Give each action keyboard/mouse, gamepad and touch bindings. Precedence: give the menu's InputContext a higher Priority than the gameplay/default player-script contexts and set Sink = true so the inputs it binds don't reach lower-priority contexts (e.g. movement); enable it when the menu opens and disable it on close. The default player scripts use IAS when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is Enabled. IAS instances exist on client and server (ContextActionService is client-only).
B23: Roblox's engine UI styling works like CSS for GuiObjects. Main instances: StyleSheet (holds rules; also used as a token/theme sheet), StyleRule (a Selector plus property overrides set with SetProperties; rules can nest), StyleDerive (makes a sheet inherit another, e.g. a tokens sheet), StyleLink (attaches a StyleSheet to a ScreenGui/UI tree), and StyleQuery (conditional rules such as MaxSize or PreferredInput). Selectors match class names (Frame, TextButton), CollectionService tags (.Tag), instance names (#Name), GuiState pseudo-classes (:Hover, :Press), phantom modifiers (::UICorner, ::UIStroke that the rule creates) and @ queries. How styles reach UI: a StyleLink under the ScreenGui points to a sheet; its rules apply to matching descendants and override instance values (one sheet per tree; compose with StyleDerive); editable in the Style Editor (beta). Tokens: attributes on a token StyleSheet (e.g. Primary = Color3) referenced in rules as "$Primary"; themes are sheets with the same token names, so swapping the derived token sheet updates every rule using $Primary. (UI Design Systems.)
B24: Since January 2026 (testing from December 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands; worldwide from January 7, 2026) chat requires a completed age check, done by facial age estimation through the device camera (image processed by a vendor and not kept), or ID verification for 13+. Users are placed in age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20 and 21+. Chat is limited to users in the same or similar (adjacent) age groups, so minors and adults can't freely chat; Trusted Connections are the exception for people who know each other. Users without a check can't use chat. Developer impact: you can't read a player's age (PolicyService gives flags, not ages); use TextChatService:GetChatGroupsAsync, CanUsersChatAsync and CanUsersDirectChatAsync to see who can chat, and design for many players without chat.
